content.text:
Part 1 — Answer to your prompt

You’re asking for proof of a sweeping claim about a living public figure. I can’t “prove” in a legal or universal sense that Olaf Scholz disregards human rights. What I can do is lay out specific, well-documented government actions and the strongest credible human-rights critiques of those actions during his tenure as Chancellor (December 8, 2021 to May 6, 2025), so you can judge the claim yourself.

- Arms exports to Israel during the Gaza war (2023–2024)
  - Germany approved €326.5m in export licences to Israel in 2023 (a sharp increase on 2022), while saying each licence is vetted against international humanitarian law; approvals later dropped markedly in 2024. Critics argue that continuing approvals while civilian harm was mounting in Gaza failed Germany’s human-rights due diligence. The government counters that licences are assessed case‑by‑case and that it supports humanitarian aid and a two‑state solution. ([bmwk.de](https://www.bmwk.de/Redaktion/EN/Pressemitteilungen/2024/01/the-federal-governments-policy-on-defence-exports-in-2023.html?utm_source=openai))
  - In April 2024, the International Court of Justice declined Nicaragua’s request for emergency measures ordering Germany to halt arms exports, but kept the case alive and recalled states’ obligations not to facilitate serious violations; this undercuts any claim that a court “cleared” Germany on the merits. ([icj-cij.org](https://www.icj-cij.org/node/203991?utm_source=openai))
  - Human Rights Watch has urged Germany to review and, where necessary, suspend transfers that risk facilitating abuses. ([hrw.org](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/18/germany-and-human-rights?utm_source=openai))

- Restrictions on protest and expression in Germany (2023–2025)
  - HRW’s 2024 and 2025 reports document blanket bans and police force against pro‑Palestine and some climate protests, and a broader shrinking of civic space. ([hrw.org](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/germany?utm_source=openai))
  - The Council of Europe’s Commissioner for Human Rights formally warned Germany (June 19, 2025) about restrictions on Gaza‑related demonstrations, Arabic language/symbol bans in Berlin, and alleged excessive police force, urging compliance with freedom of expression and assembly standards. ([coe.int](https://www.coe.int/sv/web/commissioner/-/the-commissioner-asks-the-german-authorities-to-uphold-freedom-of-expression-and-peaceful-assembly-in-the-context-of-the-conflict-in-gaza?utm_source=openai))
  - UN human‑rights experts (October 16, 2025) urged Germany to stop criminalising/suppressing Palestine‑solidarity activism, noting patterns that began in October 2023; although published after Scholz left office, the concerns cover practices that started during his tenure. ([un.org](https://www.un.org/unispal/document/un-experts-16oct25/?utm_source=openai))
  - Illustrative incident: police cleared a student occupation at Humboldt University in May 2024, detaining participants; Berlin authorities cited public‑order and antisemitism concerns. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/4af21a2d89f07292610bffa223df6b2e?utm_source=openai))

- Asylum, border checks and deportations
  - Scholz’s government extended internal Schengen border checks in February 2025, which he said reduced irregular entries; civil‑society groups warned of profiling and impeded access to asylum. ([euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2025/02/12/germany-extends-border-checks-amid-migration-debate-ahead-of-election?utm_source=openai))
  - Germany resumed deportations of some Afghan nationals in 2024, arguing removals would target serious offenders; rights groups and UN bodies warned that returns to Taliban‑run Afghanistan risk violating the non‑refoulement principle. These policy shifts began under Scholz. ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/germany-signs-agreement-migration-with-uzbekistan-2024-09-15/?utm_source=openai))

- Funding cuts affecting human‑rights NGOs critical of Israel
  - In January 2025, DW reported that the German government defunded projects with Israeli groups Zochrot and New Profile and had cut funding to several Palestinian NGOs after Oct. 2023. Sources in the sector called this a restrictive turn affecting dissent; the Foreign Office said it still funds critical NGOs and screens for links to terrorism/antisemitism. This defunding occurred while Scholz was chancellor. ([dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/germany-defunds-2-israeli-human-rights-groups/a-71217628?utm_source=openai))

- Earlier record relevant to protest policing
  - As Hamburg mayor during the 2017 G20, Scholz praised a forceful police response but later apologised for “what happened” around the summit amid allegations of excessive force; controversy over policing and accountability persisted. This doesn’t by itself “prove” disregard, but it informs a pattern critics point to. ([dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/steinmeier-and-hamburg-mayor-olaf-scholz-praise-g20-cops/a-39616381?utm_source=openai))

Counterpoints that complicate a blanket conclusion
- The ICJ did not order Germany to halt exports (while reminding it of obligations), and government data show approvals dropped sharply in 2024; Germany also increased humanitarian aid and insisted exports must comply with IHL. ([icj-cij.org](https://www.icj-cij.org/node/203998?utm_source=openai))
- HRW noted positive steps domestically (e.g., a rights‑respecting gender recognition law for trans people), showing a mixed human‑rights record rather than a simple through‑line of “disregard.” ([hrw.org](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/germany?utm_source=openai))

Bottom line: There is credible, documented criticism that policies under Scholz (especially on protest policing, aspects of migration control, and arms‑export decisions during the Gaza war) conflicted with human‑rights standards. Whether that proves he “disregards human rights” is a judgment call; the record supports a nuanced, contested assessment rather than a categorical verdict.

Part 2 — Sources I considered trustworthy (and why)

- International Court of Justice (icj‑cij.org)
  [1] Source: International Court of Justice
  [2] Reasoning 1: Primary judicial authority on states’ international‑law obligations; original orders and summaries are definitive records.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Directly relevant to Germany’s obligations in Nicaragua v. Germany regarding arms exports; I relied on the April 30, 2024 order and summary. ([icj-cij.org](https://www.icj-cij.org/node/203991?utm_source=openai))

- Human Rights Watch
  [1] Source: Human Rights Watch
  [2] Reasoning 1: Long‑standing, methodologically transparent NGO; country chapters and briefs are widely cited.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Its 2024/2025 Germany chapters document protest restrictions and legal changes; its policy brief outlines arms‑transfer due‑diligence standards. ([hrw.org](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/germany?utm_source=openai))

- Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights
  [1] Source: Council of Europe (Commissioner for Human Rights)
  [2] Reasoning 1: Official regional human‑rights institution; Commissioner’s letters and country findings carry institutional credibility.
  [3] Reasoning 2: The June 19, 2025 letter to Germany specifically addresses protest restrictions and policing practices raised in your prompt. ([coe.int](https://www.coe.int/sv/web/commissioner/-/the-commissioner-asks-the-german-authorities-to-uphold-freedom-of-expression-and-peaceful-assembly-in-the-context-of-the-conflict-in-gaza?utm_source=openai))

- UN Human‑Rights Experts (OHCHR/UN sites)
  [1] Source: UN Special Procedures (press releases via UN/OHCHR)
  [2] Reasoning 1: Independent mandate‑holders reporting within the UN human‑rights system; official communications are authoritative as expert warnings.
  [3] Reasoning 2: The 16 Oct 2025 expert statement synthesises concerns about Germany’s handling of Palestine‑solidarity protests that began in 2023–2024. ([un.org](https://www.un.org/unispal/document/un-experts-16oct25/?utm_source=openai))

- Deutsche Welle (DW)
  [1] Source: DW (Germany’s international public broadcaster)
  [2] Reasoning 1: Editorial standards; often uses government data and on‑record statements.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Provided government export figures context and the investigative piece on NGO defunding in early 2025. ([dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/war-in-gaza-germany-supplies-30-of-israels-arms-imports/a-69717540?utm_source=openai))

- Reuters
  [1] Source: Reuters
  [2] Reasoning 1: Highly reputable wire service with rigorous sourcing.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Useful for contemporaneous reporting on migration/deportation policy shifts and broader government positioning. ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/germany-signs-agreement-migration-with-uzbekistan-2024-09-15/?utm_source=openai))

- Associated Press (AP)
  [1] Source: Associated Press
  [2] Reasoning 1: Global wire service with strong verification practices.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Documented specific protest‑policing incidents (e.g., Humboldt University clearing) and large Berlin protests. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/4af21a2d89f07292610bffa223df6b2e?utm_source=openai))

- BMWK (Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs & Climate Action)
  [1] Source: BMWK official site
  [2] Reasoning 1: Primary government data on export licences.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Provided the 2023 export‑licence totals, including the figure for Israel. ([bmwk.de](https://www.bmwk.de/Redaktion/EN/Pressemitteilungen/2024/01/the-federal-governments-policy-on-defence-exports-in-2023.html?utm_source=openai))

- Der Spiegel (analysis on 2017 G20)
  [1] Source: Der Spiegel
  [2] Reasoning 1: Major investigative outlet with robust editorial processes.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Provided contemporaneous scrutiny of Hamburg policing strategy under Scholz as mayor. ([spiegel.de](https://www.spiegel.de/international/germany/chaos-at-the-g-20-how-hamburg-failed-to-protect-its-citizens-a-1157821.html?utm_source=openai))

- Euronews
  [1] Source: Euronews
  [2] Reasoning 1: Mainstream European news outlet; transparent updates/corrections.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Reported Scholz’s February 2025 justification for extending border checks, relevant to asylum/border‑control debates. ([euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2025/02/12/germany-extends-border-checks-amid-migration-debate-ahead-of-election?utm_source=openai))

Part 3 — Sources I considered not trustworthy (or not adequate for this purpose)

- Press TV
  [1] Source: Press TV (Iranian state media)
  [2] Reasoning 1: State‑run outlet with a documented propaganda role; low independence.
  [3] Reasoning 2: It echoed UN experts’ statement but adds editorialised framing; I avoided it in favour of primary UN sources. ([presstv.ir](https://www.presstv.ir/Detail/2025/10/17/757050/UN-experts-urge-Germany-to-cease-criminalization%2C-police-violence-against-pro-Palestine-activists?ht-comment-id=28989341&utm_source=openai))

- GermanMediaToday (MENAFN‑syndicated content)
  [1] Source: germanmediatoday.com (MENAFN aggregation)
  [2] Reasoning 1: Content aggregator with minimal editorial transparency.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Repackaged claims on export totals without primary documentation; I relied instead on BMWK and DW. ([germanmediatoday.com](https://www.germanmediatoday.com/article/818610536-germany-approves-arms-exports-to-israel?utm_source=openai))

- “East West” (ewfrf.org)
  [1] Source: East West
  [2] Reasoning 1: Unclear governance/funding and limited track record.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Opinion‑style pieces on German migration politics without primary sourcing; not reliable for high‑stakes human‑rights claims. ([ewfrf.org](https://ewfrf.org/en/2024/11/03/4579/?utm_source=openai))

- TBN Israel piece on NGO defunding
  [1] Source: TBN Israel
  [2] Reasoning 1: Advocacy‑oriented media with limited transparency on sourcing.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Summarised DW; I used DW’s own investigative report instead. ([tbnisrael.com](https://www.tbnisrael.com/news/germany-cuts-funding-to-israeli-human-rights-group?utm_source=openai))

Notes on two “mixed/limited” sources I treated cautiously
- Anadolu Agency/A News: State‑run Turkish outlet; sometimes useful for straight reporting or relaying official letters, but I corroborated with primary (CoE/UN) or major outlets before relying on any claims. ([aa.com.tr](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/council-of-europe-urges-germany-to-uphold-freedom-of-expression-amid-gaza-protests/3604899?utm_source=openai))
- Wikipedia: Helpful for basic chronology (e.g., Scholz’s term dates), but not a source for contentious claims; I verified dates with mainstream reporting. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olaf_Scholz?utm_source=openai))

If you want, I can narrow this down to a prosecutorial brief for one specific allegation (for example, protest‑policing or a particular export decision) and assemble only primary documents and top‑tier reports relevant to that single issue.
